We present time-series photometry of 11 hypervelocity stars (HVSs) to constrain their nature.

over 20 HVSs have been identified in the

We targeted all 12 unbound HVSs known
prior to 2008 March, plus four bound velocity outliers
from the HVS Survey of Brown et al. (2007b).

26 previously
known hypervelocity stars (HVSs) around the Milky Way.

A hypervelocity star is one whose velocity is suficiently fast that it
will escape the gravitational pull of the Milky Way.

We study 42 radial velocity outliers from the Hyper-
velocity Star Survey (Brown et al. 2007b, 2014).

Twenty one stars are significantly un-
bound in radial velocity alone (Brown et al. 2014).

We refer to bound objects
with the letter B followed by their target number in the
HVS Survey, and unbound objects by their published
HVS number.
We reanalyzed low-resolution optical spectra of 14 HVSs from the MMT HVS survey

The MMT HVS survey by Brown et al. (2014) discovered 38
late B-type HVSs, 16 of which are considered to be bound to the
Galaxy. We selected the 14 most interesting ones, that is, those
stars which have proper motions measured by HST.
sixteen of which were considered bound to the Galaxy as indicated by their name starting with the letter “B”.
It is worthwhile to also reconsider the stars originally considered unbound.
we extend the spectrophotometric analysis to 40 out of the 42 high-velocity outliers of the MMT HVS sample
for 88 known HVSs or candidates, including the 52 found in this work.
The HVS Survey detected 21 unbound B-type main-sequence
We perform this analysis for all 21 HVS Survey stars

Our targeted search for HVSs uncovered two new
HVSs, SDSS J091301.0+305120 (hereafter HVS4) and
SDSS J091759.5+672238 (hereafter HVS5).

HVS4 and HVS5 are clearly unbound to the
Galaxy.

We have repeat
observations of HVS1, HVS4, and HVS5; their radial ve-
locities are constant within the uncertainties.
